subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment qualification - hardware & offline ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Thompson <john.thompson@legacybank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 17:35:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem air-gapped deployment - post-call recap & next steps

Hi John,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the thorough walkthrough of LegacyBank's on-prem constraints. Quick recap and requested items so we can size a Private (air-gapped) proposal: 

- Primary requirement: fully air-gapped inference stack with no egress to public internet.
- Hardware baseline: current environment is 8 x A100-equivalent nodes; we'd like an exact inventory (GPU model, RAM, disk, NICs) and whether these are single-socket or dual-socket.
- Upgrade cadence: confirm maintenance window preferences (weekly windows vs quarterly major upgrades) and whether onsite staff can handle firmware/driver updates during airgap procedures.
- Offline ops: clarify patching approach (USB/airgapped media vs internal update servers) and whether you have an existing jump-host/process for software attestations.
- Logs & audits: need to understand retention requirements and if logs must be exported to a separate secure site or can be kept locally for X months.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the hardware inventory and network segmentation diagram (see attached example from another customer).
2) Our infra engineer (Dev) will review and flag any immediate incompatibilities.
3) We'll draft a tentative BOM and upgrade plan and follow up with a technical workshop next week.

Can you send the inventory and confirm an internal contact for on-site operations?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: network-segmentation-diagram.pdf (stub)
From: John Thompson <john.thompson@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@legacybank.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment - post-call recap & next steps

Marissa,

Great summary — thanks. Attaching the hardware inventory and high-level network diagram as requested. A few clarifications inline below: 

- Hardware: inventory attached (legacybank-hw-inventory.xlsx). Most GPU hosts are dual-socket, 512GB RAM, Mellanox 100Gbps NICs; GPUs are a mix of A100 40GB and A40s.
- Maintenance windows: we prefer quarterly major upgrades; monthly 4-hour maintenance windows are available for emergency patching.
- Onsite ops: Sarah (cc'd) is our lead for infrastructure and will be the primary contact for any on-site procedures. They have experience with airgap workflows and have an internal attestation process for new binaries.
- Patching: we use signed update bundles staged via an internal SFTP server on an isolated network — USB media is allowed only with dual-approval.
- Logs: must be retained locally for 12 months; export to central SIEM is allowed but only over our private replication link.

We'll be available for a technical workshop next Thursday (Aug 19) in the afternoon EST if that works for your team.

John
VP, Infrastructure
LegacyBank

Attachments: legacybank-hw-inventory.xlsx (stub); network-segmentation-diagram.pdf (stub)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: John Thompson <john.thompson@legacybank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment - post-call recap & next steps

John, Marissa,

Thanks for the inventory — having the GPU breakdown helps. A few immediate technical notes after a quick pass: 

- GPU mix: A100 40GB is fine for our recommended quantized 16/8-bit profiles; A40s will serve lower-throughput worker pools. We'll propose a split: primary serving cluster on A100s and batch/eviction workers on A40s.
- Network: 100Gbps Mellanox is sufficient but we need to validate MTU and RDMA config for our KV-cache replication. Please confirm MTU and whether RoCE v2 is enabled.
- Storage: plan for NVMe-backed local cache (1-2 TB per host) plus a separate NFS export for model artifacts if you want faster rollouts.
- Offline upgrades: we can build signed bundles for your attestation flow. We will need a temporary serial/console access plan for first-time installs (can be done via onsite engineer).

I'll prepare a short tech readout and BOM for the workshop. Marissa — can we lock in Aug 19 3:00pm EST for the tech workshop?

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Thompson <john.thompson@legacybank.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment - post-call recap & next steps

John — thanks, this is perfect. Aug 19 3:00pm EST is booked on our side for the technical workshop (calendar invite to follow).

Pre-workshop ask: can Sarah or someone from your team confirm MTU/RoCE details and share a brief sample of your signed bundle attestation metadata so Dev can validate compatibility before the call? If you can drop those two items into the shared Drive link below, Dev and Neha will incorporate them into the BOM and upgrade plan.

Shared Drive: https://redwood.app/drive/Shared/LegacyBank-MAP-4721

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll come to the workshop with a proposed node-level BOM and a step-by-step offline upgrade procedure for review.

Best,
